assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reframes intracellular organization as liquid-liquid phase separation of multivalent macromolecules, a general thermodynamic and phase-behaviour concept (P granules, nucleoli, condensates) that carries soft-matter physics into cell biology. Conceptually original and now pervasive across biochemistry, with a clear physical-chemical core.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne demonstrated liquid-like P granules and the physical framing; Rosen's multivalent-interaction phase-diagram work is the quantitative biophysical complement. Pappu, Mittag and others have strong claims, so the three-person cut is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Roughly a decade of rapid, independent confirmation, but quantitative scrutiny continues and the field is still sorting out which in-cell assemblies are genuine phase separation. Recognition would be somewhat early yet defensible.
uncertainties: Debate over whether many reported condensates are true thermodynamic phase separation versus other assemblies
Fair division among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is unclear
Disease-relevance claims are still maturing

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a lipid self-assembly and membrane-chemistry solution to nucleic-acid delivery: pH-dependent charge, bilayer and non-bilayer phase behaviour govern encapsulation and endosomal release. Enormous societal impact through siRNA and mRNA vaccines, with a physical-chemical rationale I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group and collaborators developed the formulation and ionizable-lipid principles; Anderson and Langer drove lipidoid screening and in vivo optimisation. Madden, MacLachlan and industrial lipid designers also contributed, so credit is spread and entangled with patents and companies.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at scale, with multiple independent products, so maturity is high. Timing is good, though the 2023 Medicine prize for mRNA modification may complicate how the committee views the delivery component.
uncertainties: Whether the chemistry-versus-medicine boundary and the 2023 Medicine prize affect eligibility
Attribution among academic and industrial inventors is murky
The mechanistic understanding of endosomal escape is incomplete

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy-landscape and funnel theory resolved Levinthal's paradox and gave protein folding a statistical-mechanical foundation, tied to experiments on folding mechanisms. A clean example of general physical principles organizing a complicated biological process.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic (with Bryngelson) developed funnelled landscape theory; Dill's hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model work is a closely related pillar; Fersht's experimental phi-value analysis is the experimental counterpart. The trio is plausible but Fersht and Bryngelson make attribution debatable.
assessment.maturity: Foundational and long confirmed, with decades of experimental and simulation support, though the 2024 prize for structure prediction partly overlapped the protein-folding territory. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recent AlphaFold prize and whether the committee sees folding as already honoured
Division of credit among theory and experiment contributors
Direct experimental tests of landscape shape are limited

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base into another on DNA without double-strand cleavage, using engineered deaminases and a Cas9 nickase. Innovative molecular chemistry with therapeutic consequences, building on CRISPR already recognised in 2020.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the clear intellectual leader; Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor, evolved TadA deaminase) were the leading co-inventors. Nishida and Kondo's independent deaminase fusion is an unresolved credit point.
assessment.maturity: First clinical trials and many independent replications exist, but long-term clinical outcomes are not yet known. Reasonably mature scientifically, slightly early clinically.
uncertainties: Derivative of the 2020 CRISPR prize, which may limit novelty in the committee's view
Nishida and Kondo priority is unresolved
Off-target and delivery limitations remain

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-directed self-assembly of discrete cages and capsules established design principles for thermodynamically controlled supramolecular architecture, enabling host-guest chemistry, confined reactivity and molecular recognition. Squarely about non-covalent organisation.
assessment.attribution: Fujita (square complexes and cages), Raymond (tetrahedral and coordination capsules) and Stang (supramolecular coordination assemblies) are the principal founders; Nitschke and Ward are strong later contributors.
assessment.maturity: Concept confirmed over three decades; supramolecular chemistry was recognised in 1987 and 2016, so some novelty fatigue is possible, and impact beyond the field is modest versus other candidates.
uncertainties: Distinctness from earlier supramolecular and 2025 framework prizes
Practical impact is narrower
Credit choices among five strong names are contestable

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant liquid-crystal templating of ordered mesoporous silica (M41S, MCM-41, FSM-16) used lyotropic self-assembly to build materials with tunable pores, with applications in catalysis, separation and drug delivery. The underlying surfactant phase behaviour is close to my own area.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck led the Mobil discovery; Inagaki and Kuroda reported related folded-sheet-derived mesoporous silica independently around the same time. Stucky, Zhao and Ryoo extended the family with block copolymers and carbon replicas.
assessment.maturity: Well established for over 30 years with extensive confirmation; the commercial and fundamental impact of the original material is real but may have plateaued.
uncertainties: Independent but near-simultaneous discovery complicates priority
Corporate invention versus academic credit
Impact may be judged smaller than other candidates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The nanocrystalline mesoporous TiO2 dye-sensitized cell combined interfacial charge-transfer chemistry with high-surface-area films, launching molecular photovoltaics and later perovskite devices. Highly original and widely cited, with strong interfacial physical chemistry.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 paper credits O’Regan and Grätzel; Hagfeldt contributed substantially to mechanisms and later development. A two-person prize is defensible but Hagfeldt's role could be argued.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed over three decades, though commercial impact stayed limited and perovskite work may overshadow it. Timing is long overdue.
uncertainties: Limited commercial deployment
Possible preference to recognise perovskites instead
Hagfeldt inclusion unresolved

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced-proximity degradation of target proteins via PROTACs and the discovery of cereblon as the molecular-glue target of thalidomide analogues opened a new pharmacological modality. Conceptually novel and clinically advancing, though less within my physical-chemistry sphere.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and developed PROTACs; Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target; Ciulli, Gray and others advanced the field. A coherent three-person set exists but is not unique.
assessment.maturity: Still early: first PROTAC clinical readouts are emerging and approvals are pending, so the recognition may be premature relative to other options.
uncertainties: Clinical validation incomplete
Compound discovery with PROTACs and molecular glues needing different credit
Many strong contributors excluded
